finding: No explicit exact Mars SOI-entry timestamp found in the primary mission sources and literature inspected. No independent published SOI epoch is available from this search for an event-error comparison.

sources.title: NASA's Psyche Mission to Fly by Mars for Gravity Assist
sources.finding: Reports May 15 flyby; does not specify an SOI-entry timestamp or radius convention.

sources.title: NASA's Psyche Mission Aces Mars Flyby, Targets Metal-Rich Asteroid
sources.finding: Reports May 15 closest approach and 4609 km surface altitude; no exact SOI entry. Image acquisition times are not SOI-entry events.

sources.title: Psyche Mission Description and Design Rationale
sources.finding: Mission synopsis and Mars gravity-assist navigation section give May 2026 and operations/maneuver windows relative to closest approach; no exact SOI entry found. Operational phase limits are not SOI crossings.

sources.title: JPL MDNav reconstructed spacecraft SPK
sources.finding: Binary comments identify reconstruction, centre-chain models, creation time and coverage endpoints; do not label SOI-entry/exit timestamps. Exact segment endpoints are data-structure metadata.

queries: Psyche Mars flyby May 2026 sphere of influence entry
scope_limit: Web search and listed primary sources, not an exhaustive search of internal mission documents. Unverified secondary/forum statements are not timing evidence. The NAIF web index yielded no matching timestamp/label; local pinned binary metadata supplies the segment comparison.
interpretation: The segment-start proximity to the fixed-a crossing is suggestive of a similar boundary choice during SPK construction, but its purpose is undocumented here. It is not independent confirmation of a published SOI event.
